From December 1, every Copilot Business license you sell comes with a consumption meter switched on, set by default to more than the license itself, and billed through you. This is the customer's new problem, the three sentences that explain it, the four-verb managed service that solves it, and what to charge.

## 6 · The Service in Four Verbs

This is the whole managed service. Everything else in the playbook, Tier 1 to 3, AgentCare, the Agent 365 overlay, wraps around it. It maps directly onto the FinOps Foundation's Inform, Optimize, Operate loop, and onto the controls Microsoft already shipped in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot, then Cost management.

SET

Onboarding, then quarterly

Agree a credit budget per tenant and per group. Lower the 4,000 default to the agreed limit. Alerts at 80% and 100%. Decide which services are allowed. Pick the funding source.

WATCH

Monthly, 1 to 2 hours a tenant

Read the meter. Top consumers, idle agents, spikes, users hitting limits, requests for more. Baseline for 30 to 60 days before you move a threshold.

TUNE

Monthly, re-plan quarterly

Steady users onto prepaid packs. Pre-purchase only at break-even. Retire idle agents. Route routine work to the cheaper model. Remove unused seats.

PROVE

One page, every month

Credits spent, by whom, on what, next to the outcome. Cost per user per month. Cost per resolved request for each agent. It feeds the QBR.

SETTurn the default into a decisiononboarding · 30 min in the admin center, with the customer on the call

You do

* Confirm the Azure subscription is linked to your partner billing account, so the meter is wired before the first credit burns.
* Create the spending policy. Replace the 4,000\-credit default with the limit the customer chose. Set a tenant-level limit too.
* Switch on alerts at 80% and 100% of budget. They repeat daily until reset, so route them to a mailbox someone reads.
* Review auto-apply for new services. Decide, with the customer, whether a new metered service is on by default or off until approved.
* Name the budget owner on the customer side. One person. Write it in the policy description.
* Choose the funding source for now: pay-as-you-go until there is a baseline.

Surface

Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot, then Cost management. Spending policies, user limits, policy alerts, credit-request routing, model profiles. Global or Billing Administrator creates; AI Administrator edits; AI Reader and Global Reader get the read-only dashboard, which is the role you give the customer's finance person.

Output

A one-page credit budget the customer signed: per-user limit, tenant limit, allowed services, alert recipients, budget owner, review date.

WATCHRead the metermonthly · 1 to 2 hours a tenant · a human and an export, for now

You do

* Pull consumption by user, group, agent, service and funding source. Note the top ten consumers and anyone who hit a limit.
* List every agent that consumed nothing. Idle agents are retirement candidates in TUNE.
* Flag spikes against the previous month. A user whose consumption tripled is either a champion or a runaway. Find out which.
* Collect the credit requests that came through routing. Each one is a conversation about value, not a ticket.
* In the first two months, do not move thresholds. The FinOps rule is a 30 to 60 day baseline before you set a real threshold, then set it at 110 to 120% of the baseline.

Surface

Cost management reports in the admin center; the Power Platform admin center for per-agent Copilot Studio consumption; Microsoft's Analytics Hub templates for single-tenant chargeback reports. The consumption API has refused automated calls since September 2026, so this is an export and a person until Microsoft ships the supported alternative.

Output

A meter reading: top consumers, idle agents, spikes, limit hits, requests. It becomes the first half of the PROVE page.

TUNEBuy the right credits the right waymonthly moves · quarterly re-plan

## 4 · Nobody Has Packaged It Yet

We went looking for who is already selling this to small businesses. Across roughly sixty searches and thirty-five vendor pages, here is what the market looks like in October 2026.

The dominant pattern

**A free 15 to 30 minute “set your spending policies” session.** Several Microsoft partners are giving the first step of the service away as lead generation, with no ongoing fee behind it.

The priced retainers

**Governance and adoption by the hour.** The best published example sells three monthly tiers of hours. Its scope covers telemetry reviews and says nothing about credit budgets, thresholds or re-billing.

What does not exist

**No SMB MSP publicly re-bills Copilot Credits, prices an included-credit allowance with overage, or sells a per-agent retainer.** The enterprise firms have essays and frameworks, not a priced Copilot consumption service.

Why is the market behind? Three reasons, and each one is a reason the partner wins by moving now.

* **The deadlines only just arrived.** Cowork billing started in July. The default-on date was announced on October 1\. The sandbox does not open until November 2.
* **Microsoft built the dials, not the operator.** Cost Management in the admin center has budgets, per-user limits, alerts, model routing and reports by user, group, agent and service. It does not come with anyone whose job is to turn them, and 40% of SMBs have no full-time IT person to do it.
* **There is no partner-side dashboard.** Microsoft publishes no multi-tenant cost view for partners, and since September 2026 the credit-consumption endpoint refuses automated calls. The service is a monthly export and a human for now. That is a moat for a partner with a process, and a wall for a partner waiting for a tool.

The analyst sentence that explains the whole opportunity

When AI is billed separately, buyers prefer per-seat pricing (42.3%) over consumption (36.6%), because they want an AI cost they can budget. Microsoft bills the new Copilot by consumption anyway. **The partner's product is turning the meter back into a budget.** That is the service, in one sentence. Futurum, “The Pricing Split,” August 2026.

[↑ Contents](#toc)

## 5 · The Three Sentences

Partners asked for this drawn with big crayons. Here it is. If a seller can say these three sentences without notes, the rest of this page is detail.

1

### “Your Copilot license now comes with a meter.”

The seat buys everyday Copilot. Cowork, Code, Autopilot, agents that serve people outside your license, and anything your agents do on their own run on the meter, in Copilot Credits. A credit is a penny.

2

### “The meter's default setting is bigger than the license.”

Microsoft ships new Copilot Business tenants with a 4,000-credit default per user. That is up to $40 a month on top of a $21 seat. For 100 users, the license is $2,100 and the default exposure is $4,000.

3

### “Somebody has to read the meter. That's us.”

Microsoft built the dials: budgets, per-user limits, alerts, model routing, reports by user, group and agent. It did not build anyone to turn them. The bill comes to us before it comes to you, so we are going to set the budget with you, watch it, tune it and hand you a receipt every month.

chunks.text:
### The Four-Stage Revenue Journey

Partners don't start at Stage 4\. They start where their customer is and build from there. Each stage adds a new layer of professional services revenue and expands the managed service retainer — compounding the relationship and the economics simultaneously.

Stage 1

Foundation & Adoption

What the partner builds:

Security baseline, data readiness, Copilot deployment. Prompt coaching, 1:few workshops, personal agent building sessions — users creating their own agents and sharing them with teammates.

**Pro Services:** $8K–$23K one-time  
**Retainer:** Tier 1 — $10–$15/user/mo 

Seed stage. Not all engagements are profitable — but this is where ideas start flowing and the upgrade path begins.

Stage 2

First Agent Deployed

What the partner builds:

First Copilot Studio agent — published, governed, company-wide. Personal agents from Stage 1 become managed Studio agents. The partner owns the deployment and the ongoing management.

**Pro Services:** $5K–$12K agent build  
**Retainer:** Tier 2 — $20–$25/user/mo 

The retainer becomes defensible the moment the first agent goes live.

Stage 3

Multi-Agent Operations

What the partner builds:

Multiple agents across departments. Compliance and governance layer. Agent 365 monitoring. The partner is now managing a live AI estate — not just a deployment.

**Pro Services:** $10K–$20K/year  
**Retainer:** Tier 2 (Expanded) — upper range 

Regulatory and compliance stickiness kicks in. This customer doesn't leave.

Stage 4

AI Transformation

What the partner builds:

Custom Azure AI solutions, full AI estate management, Power Platform integration. The partner is the customer's outsourced AI operations center.

**Pro Services:** $20K–$50K+/year  
**Retainer:** Tier 3 — $45–$55/user/mo 

Business continuity, not just governance. Token management, priority incident response, strategic AI advisory.

Why This Is Stickier Than Any MSP Contract You've Ever Had

Traditional MSP contracts are sticky because switching is painful. Managed AgentOps contracts are sticky because switching is **impossible without losing the entire AI estate** — every agent, every workflow, every custom prompt, every grounded knowledge base. The institutional knowledge lives in your practice. That's not a contract. That's a dependency.

### The Three-Tier Service Model

Structure Managed AgentOps as three tiers. Tiered packaging gives customers a clear entry point, gives you a natural upgrade conversation, and makes the value at each level transparent and defensible. **Agent builds are always scoped and priced separately** — the monthly retainer covers ongoing management, not new construction.

### Expand, Manage, And Prepare To Teach Customers

#### What You Do

* Run one full management cadence: exposure review, label review, shadow-AI review, access review, executive report.
* Define SOC and helpdesk handoff for AI questions, incidents, exceptions, and governance requests.
* Add quarterly label refresh and retraining to the management cadence so training does not become a one-time event.
* Package internal artifacts into clean templates: assessment deck, remediation runbook, training deck, management report.
* Use at least one anonymized internal proof asset in a real customer conversation and capture what resonated.
* Move to [Build Sellable Services](build-sellable-services.html) and map each captured artifact to an offer.

#### Tools In This Phase

Purview and SAM trend reports; Defender for Cloud Apps review; Secure Score trend; Copilot Dashboard / Viva Insights; helpdesk/SOC ticket patterns; Agent Registry or Agent 365 when agent governance maturity requires it.

#### People

**Lead:** AI owner. **Accountable:** your partner principal or executive sponsor. **Consulted:** security/compliance owner, tenant/M365 admin, helpdesk, SOC owner, delivery consultant, and practice lead. **Informed:** champions and customer-facing sales/service leaders.

#### Process

Move from project to operating cadence: review exposure, labels, shadow AI, adoption, support tickets, agent requests, and executive reporting on a recurring rhythm. The monthly executive report should be leadable in 30 seconds: one visible delta metric, one risk trend, and one recommended action. This is where the internal motion becomes the managed-service pattern.

#### Done When

You can show the before-state, explain the order of operations, prove the after-state, train a user cohort, operate a recurring cadence, refresh labels/training quarterly, use anonymized proof in a customer conversation, and describe which work becomes fixed-fee vs recurring.

#### Ready For Services

Move to the sellable-services guide when you have completed at least one full governance cadence and can show customer-safe proof for assessment, remediation, shadow AI, labels/training, adoption, and management.

#### Capture

Trend report, SLA, recurring tasks, quarterly retraining plan, packaging notes, delivery-readiness gaps, customer-conversation notes, anonymized proof.

## Training And Enablement Are Part Of The Build

## 10\. The Revenue Model That Makes the Climb Worth It

**A note on what follows:** The revenue model described in this section — and particularly the concept of Managed AgentOps — represents one way of thinking about the AI services opportunity. These ideas are grounded in channel data and research, but they are not an official Microsoft program or framework, and no single approach is right for every partner business. Think of this as a mental model for structuring recurring AI services revenue, not a mandate. For the full breakdown — including a stage-by-stage customer scenario, revenue benchmarks, and the research behind the numbers — the [Copilot Partner Playbook](https://copilotplaybook.com/cpb.html) goes considerably deeper. 

Every tier on the partner ladder unlocks a higher level of capability — but capability only matters if it translates into revenue. The partners winning in the Microsoft channel right now aren't just climbing toward Frontier for the badge. They are building a fundamentally new business model underneath it: **Managed AgentOps.**

📖

Full Deep Dive Available

This section is the executive summary. The [Copilot Partner Playbook](https://copilotplaybook.com/cpb.html) is the operating manual — with the complete First Community Bank customer scenario, stage-by-stage revenue tables, AgentOps argument for each stage, and the full benchmark validation against Forrester and IDC research.

[Read the Playbook →](https://copilotplaybook.com/cpb.html) 

$8.45

per $1 of Copilot licensing

The multiplier that changes everything.

For every $1 of Microsoft Copilot licensing sold, service-focused partners generate **$8.45 in their own services revenue** — across security, adoption, agent builds, and managed operations. This is the economic foundation the entire revenue model is built on. Source: IDC #US52483124, commissioned by Microsoft

Two Revenue Streams — One Copilot Conversation

The Copilot opportunity produces two distinct revenue streams that **stack, not compete.**

🔧 Stream 1 — Professional Services

Security readiness, data governance, adoption workshops, custom agent builds. **One-time or project-based.** This is what most partners already know how to sell — and it funds the relationship that earns the retainer.

🔁 Stream 2 — Managed AgentOps

The ongoing management layer of the customer's AI estate. Prompt tuning, data grounding, token governance, security posture, AI ROI reviews. **Recurring, sticky, and unlike anything the channel has seen before.**

### The Four-Stage Revenue Journey

Partners don't start at Stage 4\. They start where their customer is and build from there. Each stage adds a new layer of professional services revenue and expands the managed service retainer — compounding the relationship and the economics simultaneously.

# The 40-Minute Cowork Session

Your complete guide — the conversation, the tools, the licensing, and what comes next.

For **partners running the Cowork conversation** · Customer Zero: Copilot Practice Builder Workshop

Do not sell Cowork. _Sell the management of Cowork._

Forty minutes is exactly enough time to make that sentence stick — if you leave with the lineup in your head, the reframe on your tongue, a real number on paper, and a named customer on your index card.

---

## 0\. The Conversation Map

Before the minute-by-minute detail, see the whole shape at once: seven beats inside the 40 minutes, then the branch you should be walking toward the moment you finish. Nothing below is optional filler — every box on this map gets its own fully-scripted stop in Section 4, and the branch at the right gets its own roadmap in Section 11.

TOTAL RUNTIME — 40 MINUTES 1 Provocation 2 The 3 Surfaces 3 Shadow AI Wedge 4 Same Model Reframe 5 The Cost Story 6 The SOW Menu 7 30-Day Contract WHAT'S NEXT — THE ARR LADDER Assessment → AUP → Managed Governance → Insurance Readiness → vCISO Retainer — training runs under every rung See Section 11 for the full roadmap & pricing 

Figure 0 — Beats 1–3 (teal) place Cowork on the map and open the governance wedge. Beats 4–5 (dark teal) survive the two objections that actually kill deals. Beats 6–7 (purple) convert the sale into a named next step — which is also where the session hands off into the six-rung ARR ladder that runs for months afterward.

[↑ Back to Table of Contents](#toc)

---

## 1\. Purpose & Outcomes

Forty minutes is not enough time to teach Cowork. It's enough time to give you the four moves you need to have the conversation — and this design is built around exactly those four, in order. This guide picks up exactly where the Shadow AI discovery conversation leaves off: your customer has a Copilot license, or is about to, and now you have to decide what to say about Cowork.

By the end, you can

**(a)** explain Cowork's place in the customer conversation without a demo, **(b)** run the co-sell talk track against a Claude or ChatGPT preference, **(c)** size Cowork consumption for a customer's monthly bill on paper, and **(d)** name the two follow-on SOWs you'll pursue after any Cowork sale.

Everything below is a building block, deliberately. Each stop in Section 4 is independently reusable in a one-on-one customer meeting, a lunch-and-learn, or a QBR — if you only retain Stop 4 (the reframe) or Stop 5 (the cost story), you still walk out able to run half the conversation.

[↑ Back to Table of Contents](#toc)

---

## 2\. Before You Walk In — the Tools You'll Actually Use

This conversation is deliberately low-tech in delivery — no live tenant, no login risk — but it leans on four real tools you'll use _live_, not just cite afterward. Know each one cold before you walk in.

### The Revenue Runway: One Bank, Four Stages

These revenue streams don’t replace each other — they stack. The partner who treats Copilot as a license sale captures a fraction of this. The partner who wraps it in services captures all of it.

| Stage                  | Pro Services                           | Managed Service (Annual)        | Cumulative Engagement              |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| **Stage 1** (Year 1)   | $8K–$23K (deployment + security)       | \~$7.2K (Tier 1, 50 users)      | \~$15K–$30K                        |
| **Stage 2** (Year 1–2) | $3.5K–$8K (agent build)                | \~$12K (Tier 2, 50 users)       | \~$19K–$28K                        |
| **Stage 3** (Year 1–2) | $25K–$45K (full integration + Phase 2) | $13K–$16.5K (AgentOps retainer) | $35K–$55K (Yr 1); $28K–$40K (Yr 2) |
| **Stage 4** (Year 2+)  | $30K–$75K+ (custom AI)                 | \~$45K (Tier 3, 75 users @ $50) | $55K–$90K+/year                    |

💡 3-Year Engagement Value from a Single SMB Bank Customer

**$75,000–$110,000 at the Stage 3 level — and substantially more if the customer reaches Stage 4.** Start at Stage 1\. The deployment engagement funds the sales process and establishes the relationship. Stage 2 proves AI’s value with the first agent. Stage 3 delivers the transformative business solution the bank actually needs. Stage 4 makes you irreplaceable. Each stage creates the pipeline for the next — and the partner who starts this journey is the only one positioned to finish it.

Microsoft Commerce Incentives (MCI)

Microsoft-Funded Deployment Programs — Quick Guide

$1,750–$10,000+

per qualifying deployment

Microsoft offers **$1,750–$10,000+ per qualifying Copilot deployment** through its Commerce Incentives (MCI) program — designed to help partners offset delivery costs and accelerate adoption. This money is available now. Most eligible partners are not claiming it.

Are You Eligible?

You’re likely ready to claim if you meet all four of these:

Enrolled in the **Microsoft Commerce Incentives (MCI)** program via Partner Center

Hold a **Solutions Partner designation** in Modern Work or Security — or have at least 25 capability points in one of those areas

At least **$25K in CSP revenue** in the past 12 months (per solution area)

Customer is purchasing **Copilot or Power Platform licenses via CSP** — net-new or upsell only

**Don’t check all four yet?** You’ve got a few steps to take — and they’re worth it. Each box you tick also moves you toward Solutions Partner and Frontier Badge eligibility.
